## Setting Up

The position of the particle is given parametrically:
$$x(t) = 3\sin\frac{t}{4}, \qquad y(t) = 3\cos\frac{t}{4}$$

The **speed** is the magnitude of the velocity vector, i.e., 
$$\text{speed} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)^2}$$

## Step 1: Differentiate with respect to $t$

Using the chain rule (with $\frac{d}{dt}\frac{t}{4} = \frac{1}{4}$):

$$\frac{dx}{dt} = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{4}\cos\frac{t}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\cos\frac{t}{4}$$

$$\frac{dy}{dt} = 3 \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)\sin\frac{t}{4} = -\frac{3}{4}\sin\frac{t}{4}$$

## Step 2: Compute the speed

$$\text{speed} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{4}\cos\frac{t}{4}\right)^2 + \left(-\frac{3}{4}\sin\frac{t}{4}\right)^2}$$

$$= \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}\cos^2\frac{t}{4} + \frac{9}{16}\sin^2\frac{t}{4}}$$

## Step 3: Simplify using the Pythagorean identity

Since $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:

$$\text{speed} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}\left(\cos^2\frac{t}{4} + \sin^2\frac{t}{4}\right)} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3}{4}$$

The speed is constant — the particle travels around a circle of radius 3, completing one revolution every $8\pi$ units of time, giving circumference $6\pi$ over period $8\pi$, hence speed $\frac{6\pi}{8\pi} = \frac{3}{4}$. ✓

$$\boxed{\dfrac{3}{4}}$$
